_purpose: Products never offered as a RECOMMENDATION, because they are formulated for children (Luneth 2026-07-16: "no adult is ever going to take those… kids will never use our app"). Editorial CURATION config — OURS, not a Wallach claim and not a pillar projection — so it lives here hand-authored (manifest 'accounted') rather than derived. It changes only what we SHOW; it never touches a target, a dose, or a composition.
_scope: Excluded from EVERY recommendation/suggestion surface: the Coverage recommendations, condition pages, and the element/entity detail view's BEST SOURCES. The ONE place they remain fully present is the products database (the Knowledge drawer's Products tab), where they stay discoverable — that surface reads essentialSlugsByProduct(), which is deliberately NOT filtered. Enforced by the `kids_products_not_recommended` invariant.
_evidence_note: Identified from Youngevity's own product copy + label panels — NEVER from the product NAME. A name heuristic was rejected because it both over- and under-fires: 'Kidney & Bladder Support' matches 'kid'; 'FlexeoPlus' says 'grandkids' (a product FOR grandparents); 'Toddy' is a drink name, not 'toddler' (Ultra Body Toddy and Cal Toddy are ADULT); and cheri-mins / strawberry-kiwi-mins carry NO kid token in their names at all. Verified 2026-07-16 by reading all 217 label images (only kids-toddy's panel is age-banded) and sweeping all 215 marketing descriptions (which is where 3 of the 4 are identifiable).
_names_deliberately_absent: Only product_id is stored. The display name lives in the Products pillar and is resolved from it; re-storing it here would be a second home for a pillar fact that silently drifts if Youngevity renames a product (R3). The gate resolves every id below against eden/products/products.json and REDs on an unknown one — a typo cannot silently un-exclude a kids product.

excluded.evidence: Label doses by AGE BAND — two %DV columns, "1/2 fl. oz. (Ages 1-3)" and "1 fl. oz. (Ages >=4)", with the child-calorie footnote "based on a 1,000 calorie diet for children 1-3 years of age". The only age-banded panel among all 217 labels. YGY copy: designed to support "your child's development from their first year" through "their early teen years".

YGY copy is explicitly child-directed: "Do your kids HATE taking their vitamins?" and "formulated to provide children with a variety of nutrients needed for healthy growth". Its LABEL is single-column on the ordinary adult 2,000-calorie basis, so the panel alone does not settle it (read + arithmetically checked against both FDA DV tables 2026-07-16 — it matches the ages-4+ table 12/12). The copy is the evidence.

YGY copy is explicitly child-directed: "ensure the kids get the essential nutrients they need to grow and thrive", "No more tantrums", "let them get back to playtime". Label is adult-looking (single %DV column, 2,000-calorie basis) because the formula IS the adult Plant Derived Minerals composition — kid-marketed, not kid-formulated. Unfindable by label or by name; identified from the copy alone.

YGY copy is explicitly child-directed — the same kid-marketed copy as cheri-mins ("ensure the kids get the essential nutrients", "No more tantrums", "back to playtime"), plus "parents want to make sure their kids are getting nutrients". Same adult-looking label + same Plant Derived Minerals composition. Unfindable by label or by name.

_considered_and_kept: Three DUAL-AUDIENCE products were reviewed and deliberately NOT excluded, because Luneth's rule is "only the explicitly kids products" and each names adults outright: bone-building-formula ("helps teens and young adult women"), sta-clear ("formulated for teenagers and adults"), ultimate-multi-efa ("the optimal health of adults and children"). Recorded here so a future session sees they were examined, not missed.
